module_title: Mechanisms, Kinematic Pairs, and Degrees of Freedom
introduction: At this level, we cover the fundamental building blocks of machines: Links, Kinematic Pairs, and the formulas used to calculate the Degree of Freedom (Mobility) of any given mechanism.

core_concepts.title: Kinematic Pairs
core_concepts.description:
1. Lower Pair: When two links have surface (area) contact between them. (e.g., Sliding pair, Turning pair, Screw pair).
2. Higher Pair: When two links have a point or line contact between them. (e.g., Cam and Follower, Gears, Ball bearings).

core_concepts.title: Degree of Freedom (DOF / Mobility - F)
core_concepts.description:
The number of independent independent coordinates required to completely specify the position of a mechanism. 
Kutzbach/Gruebler's Criterion for planar mechanisms: 
F = 3(L - 1) - 2J - H 
(Where L = number of links, J = number of lower pairs/binary joints, H = number of higher pairs).

core_concepts.title: Grashof's Law
core_concepts.description:
For a planar 4-bar linkage to have continuous relative motion (at least one link capable of making a full 360-degree revolution), the sum of the shortest (s) and longest (l) links must be less than or equal to the sum of the other two links (p and q). 
Condition: s + l <= p + q

important_entities.name: Kinematic Inversions
important_entities.significance: The method of obtaining different mechanisms by fixing different links in a kinematic chain is known as inversion. (e.g., Inverting a slider-crank chain yields the hand water pump, oscillating cylinder engine, and Whitworth quick return mechanism).

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Exam Trap: If you calculate DOF and get F = 0, it is NOT a mechanism; it is a Frame or Structure with no relative motion (like a bridge truss). If F = -1, it is a Super Structure (statically indeterminate).

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Gear teeth meet at a line (Higher pair), whereas a piston rubs against a cylinder with its entire surface (Lower pair).

exam_strategy_tips: A patent SSC JE theoretical question: 'What type of kinematic pair is formed by a Cam and Follower?' Answer: Higher Pair.
